actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

device.name: Semantic Digital Twin panda single-cube scene (MuJoCo)

facts.text: The package is a world model that unifies kinematic information and semantic meaning for robotic world representations
The package's adapters import scenes in formats including URDF, USD and MJCF
The scene is the MuJoCo MJCF model named 'panda scene'
The scene compiles angles in radians and derives limits automatically (autolimits true)
The panda default class gives its joints the range -2.8973 to 2.8973 rad, armature 0.1 and damping 1
The panda default class gives general actuators the control range -2.8973 to 2.8973 and force range -87 to 87
The panda default class gives position actuators the force range -100 to 100
The finger default class gives finger joints the slide type on axis 0 1 0 and the range 0 to 0.04 m
The arm is the body chain link0 to link7 with the hinge joints joint1 to joint7
joint2 has the range -1.7628 to 1.7628 rad
joint4 has the range -3.0718 to -0.0698 rad
joint6 has the range -0.0175 to 3.7525 rad
The hand carries the two slide joints finger_joint1 and finger_joint2, both of the finger class
An equality constraint couples finger_joint1 and finger_joint2
The actuator section declares seven position actuators for joint1 to joint7 and one general actuator for finger_joint1
actuator1 and actuator3 have the control range -2.8973 to 2.8973 rad and actuator2 has -1.7628 to 1.7628 rad
actuator4 has the control range -3.0718 to -0.0698 rad and actuator5 has -2.8973 to 2.8973 rad
actuator6 has the control range -0.0175 to 3.7525 rad
actuator7 is the position actuator for joint7 and states no control range of its own
actuator8 is the general actuator for finger_joint1 with the control range 0 to 0.04 m
The integration step is 0.005 s and the integrator is implicitfast with 5 iterations and 8 line-search iterations
The custom numeric max_contact_points is 12
The scene has a static plane floor and a free-floating box body of size 0.02 0.02 0.03 m
The keyframes home, pickup and pickup1 each give 16 qpos values and 8 ctrl values
The upstream test suite loads this exact MJCF file
The upstream MJCF adapter parses a scene with mujoco.MjSpec.from_file
The upstream MJCF adapter iterates the spec's actuators when building its world
The package requires Python 3.10 or newer

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from mj_resetData and the model has no random element, so a fixed ctrl sequence and tick count repeat the trajectory.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the model's integration step, joint dimensions and actuator control ranges and moves each actuated joint toward its control target; it computes no inertias, contacts, equality constraints or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is an engine result
the box's free joint and the finger equality constraint are not simulated: the box qpos values stay at zero, and only finger_joint1 is actuated, so finger_joint2 stays at zero instead of following it
the bridge reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults (zero qpos in the stand-in), not from the home, pickup or pickup1 keyframes of the model

the upstream simulation adapter uses the external Multiverse connector (mujoco_connector) in src/semantic_digital_twin/adapters/multi_sim.py, which this package neither installs nor runs; the package serves the MJCF model directly through the MujocoBridge
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is exposed
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's 5 ms step only
the model is a simulation asset: no physical robot is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against hardware
MuJoCo is not installed where the acceptance gate runs, so the stand-in was not compared with an engine load of this model

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
